correctness.rationale: For all integer d>=1, 0<sigma<tau, 0<w<1, direct differentiation gives Hessian -uI+delta^2*t/(1+t)^2*xx^T with u>0, t=r*exp(-delta*norm(x)^2/2). Its radial eigenvalue has the sign of log(r)-F_q(t), and F_q has a unique global minimum at t=q/(1+sqrt(1+q(q+1))). The closed-form minimum yields precisely r<=R(q) without omitted boundaries. Endpoint and infinity Hessian limits yield strong convexity strictly below threshold. Linear projection whitening is exact. The 4D-versus-3D rational witness is certified by elementary exponential bounds. The packaged standalone program also compares exact derivative identities and direct numerical Hessians (3,042 checks); finite checks do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: A sharp necessary-and-sufficient log-concavity classification for a common two-point Gaussian scale-mixture model addresses a nontrivial stability problem for mixtures. The dimension effect gives a natural all-proper-linear-marginals counterexample to the converse of the marginal log-concavity preservation principle, including a low-dimensional rational-weight witness. It identifies exactly when a unimodal density is not log-concave and where curvature fails; not merely a numerical slice, tautological reformulation, or unmotivated invariant. Existing moment and entropy bounds do not imply its sharp global curvature transition.
